conversion.exporter: scripts/make_fp16.py (calls the shipping export.export_rfdetr._to_fp16, then export.fp16_repair.repair)

notes: Candidate. Never deployed, never in S3; the declared target names the only host these bytes have ever executed on, so measuredOnTarget being true here is tautological, not an endorsement. It is false on the serving record, which is the comparison worth reading. Promoting these bytes would be a new record, with parity re-measured on the real target.

The class list and both recommended thresholds are inherited from the fp32 sidecar - there is no fp16 sidecar. confThresholdRecommended=0.4 was reasoned about against fp32 behaviour; what inheriting it costs on these bytes is in parity.comparison.atRecommendedThreshold, not in an argument.

IO stays FLOAT (keep_io_types=True), so the fp16 boundary is inside the graph and the consumer contract is unchanged. That is a decision, and it is in the identity tuple via io.input.dtype - while precisionEvidence shows the weights underneath are FLOAT16.
Raw converter output does not load in ONNX Runtime for this graph; export.fp16_repair is part of the mechanism, not a post-hoc fix, and these bytes are the repaired ones.

Measured on macOS 26.5.1; the int8 record's evidence was gathered on 26.6.2 (same architecture, same onnxruntime 1.29.0, same execution provider). The two candidates were therefore not measured under identical conditions, and their divergence numbers should not be compared to each other as if they were.
Stored under dist/, which is gitignored: verify will report MISSING on a fresh clone. The sha256 is the artifact's identity; the path is only where it was last seen.
